brief.product: Cal.com scheduling platform with booking pages, team scheduling, routing, workflows, embeds and Platform API, plus Cal Video, Events, Cal.ai and integrations.
brief.positioning: Cal.com is scheduling software that replaces email back-and-forth with one booking link, offering one calendar for every way people meet for individuals, teams and enterprises.
differentiators: Open source and customizable scheduling infrastructure
Built-in Cal Video with browser guest join, recording and transcription on a team plan
100+ app integrations including Slack and Salesforce
Free for individuals with unlimited links and no usage limits

audiences.name: Solo professionals and small-business owners sharing booking links
pains: Finding a time took a week of emails. Now it's one link.
Whenever I share a Calendly link over email, the conversation tends to die down.
jobsToBeDone: Share one link instead of trading availability by email
Start scheduling free without usage limits
objections: A link may feel too impersonal for a client relationship
Scheduling tools can get expensive or complicated as usage grows

audiences.name: Enterprise recruiting coordinators and operations teams
pains: Calendly works fine for first-round screens. But once you hit panel interviews or custom workflows, it breaks.
jobsToBeDone: Coordinate complex team and panel scheduling without manual follow-up
Have bookings show up in Slack, Salesforce, and tools the team already uses
objections: A basic scheduler may not hold up beyond simple one-to-one meetings
Efficiency claims need proof from a comparable company, not general promises

audiences.name: Service businesses with staff, services, and paid bookings
pains: The bill scaling per seat, reminders being metered or gated, booking pages that are 'functional but visually rigid' and hard to change.
jobsToBeDone: Let customers book staff and services online without rigid pages or surprise limits
Start free and move to a collaborative plan only when the company size requires it
objections: Key no-show and page-customisation features may be gated or hard to adapt

competitors.name: Calendly
competitors.howWeDiffer: Calendly is the polished mainstream benchmark with routing forms and a large integration ecosystem. Cal.com differs on evidence as an open-source scheduling platform that is free for individuals with no usage limits; do not claim Cal.com has a larger ecosystem than Calendly.

competitors.name: SavvyCal
competitors.howWeDiffer: SavvyCal is positioned around invitee-first booking UX with calendar overlay for busy calendars and teams. Cal.com's evidenced contrast is breadth of meeting format: one calendar for every way people meet, including built-in Cal Video where guests join from the browser without an account.

competitors.name: TidyCal
competitors.howWeDiffer: TidyCal is positioned as the budget-friendly lifetime-deal option for individuals and solos. Cal.com is honestly not a lifetime deal: individuals are free forever with no usage limits, while collaborative features are paid per-user plans, so the difference is a free unlimited start plus a team upgrade path.

competitors.name: YouCanBookMe
competitors.howWeDiffer: YouCanBookMe is positioned on customizable booking pages, intake forms, and tailored booking communications integrated with Google Calendar. Cal.com's evidenced difference is open-source scheduling infrastructure and bookings surfacing in Slack, Salesforce, and 100+ other tools; do not claim its pages are more customizable without proof.

competitors.name: Acuity Scheduling
competitors.howWeDiffer: Acuity Scheduling is positioned for appointment-based service businesses managing appointments online. Cal.com's evidenced difference is a broader one-calendar proposition for individuals, teams, and enterprises, with Cal Video built into each booking; do not claim deeper appointment-service specialisation than Acuity.

pillars.name: One link, not a week of emails
pillars.purpose: Connect the pain of email back-and-forth and conversations dying after a link is shared to Cal.com's one-link booking outcome.

pillars.name: One calendar for every way people meet
pillars.purpose: Connect varied meeting formats and video friction to one calendar plus built-in Cal Video rooms that guests join from the browser without an account.

pillars.name: Bookings where your team already works
pillars.purpose: Connect complex team and panel workflows breaking in basic schedulers to bookings showing up in Slack, Salesforce, and 100+ connected tools.

pillars.name: Start free, pay only to collaborate
pillars.purpose: Connect per-seat cost anxiety and gated features to a free start with no usage limits, with premium plans chosen to fit company size.

pillars.name: Proof time goes back to real work
pillars.purpose: Connect time lost to scheduling to Deel's cited 35% reduction in scheduling time and 20% improvement in meeting attendance, framed as one customer's result.

voiceRules: Lead with the pain, then the fix in one short sentence.
Use plain, everyday words; avoid enterprise jargon.
Keep each line to one clear benefit or outcome.
Write for absolutely everyone, not just big teams.
Be warm and human; never cold, hyped, or pushy.
Use ambitious mission language only as aspiration.
exclusions: Do not present Deel's 35% scheduling-time reduction or 20% attendance improvement as a guaranteed or typical result for every customer.
Do not claim Cal.com is #1, best, or better-rated than any competitor; the evidence lists alternatives and ratings but proves no superiority.
Do not claim unproven security, compliance, uptime, or enterprise procurement credentials; no such evidence is supplied.
Do not claim unlimited collaborative or team features for free; the site says collaborative features require a premium plan.
Do not claim recording and transcription are available on every plan; the site ties them to a team plan.
Do not disparage competitors as broken for all users; the panel-interview pain is one cited enterprise recruiting view.
Do not use hyped, salesy, or exclusionary language that conflicts with 'Scheduling for absolutely everyone.'
businessObjectives: Grow free individual sign-ups as the entry point to team adoption
Move collaborative teams to paid Teams or Organizations plans
Prove scheduling time savings with named customer outcomes such as Deel
campaignObjectives: Make the cost of email back-and-forth immediately relatable
Demonstrate one link, one calendar, and built-in video in plain language
Convert social attention into a free start with no usage limits
brief.intendedConversion: Start scheduling for free with no credit card and no usage limits

claims.text: Making time for millions of people every month.
Finding a time took a week of emails. Now it's one link.
Connects to Slack, Salesforce, and 100+ more. Bookings show up where your team already works.
Start scheduling for free, with no usage limits. For collaborative features, choose one of our premium plans that fits your company size.

Cal Video is the video calling built into Cal.com. Each booking gets a room at its own link, guests join from the browser without an account, and on a team plan the call can be recorded and transcribed.

Deel has seen a 35% reduction in the time spent on scheduling meetings since they started using Cal.com . In addition to that, they have also seen a 20% improvement in overall meeting attendance rates. These efficiency gains mean that Deel now has more time to focus on other value-added tasks, like maintaining market leadership in their industry and fostering innovation.
